task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_hydra_: Hydra's soldiers guard their bases in armed squads. Take one down before the alarm goes up.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_ice_dr: Snow Wraiths live in snowy and frozen biomes. Their breath freezes you in place, so keep moving.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_lightn: Skrills live in swamps, jungles, savannas and badlands. You usually hear the strike before you see the dragon.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_sea_se: Sea Serpents hunt the oceans, Elythia's included. In the water it is much stronger than you.
It lurks in Cavaryn's Toxic Caves. Set it on fire first, or every head you cut off grows back as two.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_cyclop: A cyclops herds sheep across the meadows and plains. Hit it in the eye to blind it, and don't let it pick you up.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_dread_: Liches raise the dead in the Dread Barrens and the frozen mausoleums. Kill the Lich first.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_stymph: Flocks roost in Thoraxis's Nadir Forest and shoot metal feathers at anything below them.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_torete: It guards the coliseum in an Elythia ocean and fires water from its shell.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_king.d: He lives alone in a great tree in Elythia's meadows. Break one of his Decrees and you lose half your hearts.
She waits below the castle in the Underside. She fights with gravity, and at the end she slows time.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_viltru: Lucan, Vidor and Thula fly in together and fight until somebody's dead. Draw a Call of Viltrum circle in the Overworld to bring them, or wait for them to come on their own. Each one drops a Viltrumite Blood Sample.
He's far stronger than the squad. He answers a Challenge of Conquest circle, cast at night in the Overworld. Scourge Virus potions poison him, and he drops three Blood Samples.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_nightm: Nightmares roam Thoraxis's Nightmare Wastes. It hits harder the lower your health gets.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_empero: It rules the Dream Dunes in Thoraxis. Its stinger goes into Big Bertha.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_hercul: It marches with the hordes in Cavaryn and charges hard enough to shake the ground.
Lucids hunt the Lucid Pools in Thoraxis. Their eyes are worth keeping.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_mantic: Manticores prowl the Dream Dunes in Thoraxis, and they serve the Queen.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_vortex: Vortexes roam the Vortex Expanse in Thoraxis. Their charges are worth keeping.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_alpha_: It leads the mantises in Elythia's meadows and Truffalo forests.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_basili: Basilisks hunt Elythia's Ouranwood forests. Don't let one look at you for long.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_brutal: It sleeps in a cocoon under the Ouranwood canopy until something damages it.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_strato: Stratosharks swim through Elythia's Cloud Sea. Watch the clouds below you.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_worm.d: Worms tunnel through Cavaryn's Wormy Caves and come up under your feet.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_entomb: Something built a resin hive in Thoraxis, and the tall one guards it. Its blood is acid.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_horned: He answers a Wicker Man built from Blood-Stained Hay and set alight. Werewolves call him to prove themselves.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_devour: A Cosmic Worm from the Starlit Factory calls it down. It is very long, and all of it wants you dead.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_wither: Nobody finds a Wither. Someone builds one from soul sand and three wither skeleton skulls. Do it far from home.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_ender_: She circles the island in the End. Break the crystals on the towers first.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_warden: It wakes in the Deep Dark when something makes noise. It is blind, so be quiet.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_electr: Some Lucky Blocks hold a dancer with a lightning act. Keep moving, because the floor gets charged.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_elder_: Three of them guard every ocean monument. Kill them and the mining fatigue stops.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_luxtru: A huge dinosaur that lives by the volcanoes in Elythia's Primordial Caves. It throws burning rock.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_hullbr: It patrols the Abyssal Chasm far below the sea floor, and it is big enough to break a submarine.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_forsak: It hunts the pitch-black Forlorn Hollows in Cavaryn, and it is far bigger than anything else down there.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_sky_ca: It flies and it is heavily armed. Some Cog Chambers have one waiting.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_scamp_: An armored tank. Expect a lot of gunfire and very little cover.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_lilith: Pour chicken blood from a Wine Glass onto a skull at night, under open sky, with chalk and candles. She can't be killed, so fight her until she yields.
Draw Death reversed in a tarot reading, or bind six of each spirit to a Clay Effigy. Either way, he comes.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_arming_u: Every gun starts at a Gun Bench. A Flintlock Pistol is the easiest one to build.
task.integrated_boogaloo.engineering_gar: Every car, truck and plane is put together at a Vehicle Bench. Start with a Camaro. It comes off the bench with its engine already in, but nothing else.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.iron: Every early Iron Man suit, Mark 1 through Mark 7.
War Machine and the Iron Patriot.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.hall: Every Iron Man suit and everything built from them.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.hero: Every Wolverine costume, with and without sleeves.
Captain America and everyone who has carried the shield.
Cyclops, Quicksilver, Captain Marvel, Deadpool and the Winter Soldier.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.asse: Every hero costume in one closet.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.star: Every weapon the Starlit Factory can forge.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.weap: Mjolnir, Stormbreaker and the Royal Guard's weapons.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.lege: Every legendary weapon, and Big Bertha.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.guns: Antique, copper, iron, frontier and treated brass guns.
Deep dark, titanium, end, ocean and piglin guns.
The scorched and wrecker guns, the strangest on the bench.
Every gun on the bench, and the Orbital Railgun.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.eggs: Spawn eggs for every creature in the Overworld, from the surface to the deep caves. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
Spawn eggs for every creature in the Nether. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
Spawn eggs for every creature in the End, the dragon included. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
Spawn eggs for every creature in Elythia. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
Spawn eggs for every creature in Cavaryn. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
Spawn eggs for every creature in Thoraxis and the Underside. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
Spawn eggs for creatures from the smaller, stranger dimensions. Dried spawn eggs are buried in the deep stone of every world. Mine one and cook it in a Blast Furnace to find out what's inside.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.all_: A spawn egg for every creature there is. Easter Bunnies lay them, and dried spawn eggs turn up in the rock.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.hats: Top hats, caps and everyday headwear.
Hats for every holiday on the calendar.
Animals that ride on your head.
Food, furniture and things that shouldn't be hats.
Headwear for angels, demons and aliens.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.ever: Every hat there is. Some mobs spawn wearing one and drop it when you beat them.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.pets: Pets that do a job: carry things, fight beside you, or keep your tools in order.
Creature pets come from witchcraft rituals: a Poppet, a few offerings, and the creature itself.
Pets made from the sky, the dimensions, and stranger places.
The odd ones. Some of these take real effort to make.
Pets for holidays and special occasions.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.reco: Music you won't find anywhere else.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.gara: One of every car model. Any paint job counts.
The Fire Truck, the Brigadier and the Renault FT.
Every plane and helicopter. Any paint job counts.
task.integrated_boogaloo.collection.all_: One of every car, truck and aircraft model.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_smoothbo: Stone guns like the Musket need no metal at all. They hold one shot, then you reload.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_gun_part: Firing units, barrels and magazines are made from nickel at a crafting table. Almost every gun past this point needs them.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_copper_r: Bullets are made at a crafting table, not the Gun Bench. An Assembler turns out twice as many from the same materials.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_iron_fra: Each frame metal opens up a new set of guns. Some fire once per click and some keep going while you hold the trigger.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_kit_it_o: Hold a gun and open the attachment screen to fit scopes, silencers, stocks, grips and bigger magazines.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_shell_ga: A shotgun throws a spread of pellets, so get close. If a gun takes more than one kind of ammo, you can swap between them.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_upkeep.d: Guns wear out as you use them. Fix one by combining it with a Repair Kit on an anvil.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_asgharia: Titanium makes the Titanium Gun Frame, and the Krauser is one of the guns built on it.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_battery_: Laser guns fire the Energy Core itself. When it runs dry, recharge it in an Assembler with redstone.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_plasma.d: A Plasma Core only comes out of an Assembler. The guns built on it fire Plasma Cells.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_flare_up: Fire a flare from the Flare Pistol to start a raid. Each kind of flare calls a different one.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_sentry.d: A Basic Turret is built from a Turret Platform and a gun. Once it's placed, it guards the area on its own.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_scorched: Scorched Ingots only come out of the Atomic Forge. They make the last frame tier and the strongest guns.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_dying_st: The Starlit Factory forges celestial weapons and burns Stardust as fuel. The longer a recipe takes, the more fuel it uses.
task.integrated_boogaloo.armory_celestia: Every celestial weapon has one skill on right-click and another while sneaking. Read its tooltip before you swing it at anything.
Aim through the scope and pick a spot. Thirty-five seconds later, everything around it from bedrock to sky is gone.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_tear_in_t: Rifts float in the air in odd places, often inside small stone gateways. A Rift Remover, made from gold ingots and an ender pearl, closes a rift and any others near it.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_loose_thr: Every rift you close with a Rift Remover drops one World Thread, and some structure chests have it too. Spin three thread with a Woven Cruor at a Spinning Wheel to make Stable Fabric.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_rift_blad: Spin a Rift Blade from an iron sword and two ender pearls. It opens a temporary door on any rift and has a teleporting attack.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_through_t: Walk through a Wood Dimensional Door
Dimensional doors are made from Antimetal, a Lucid Pearl and an ordinary door. Place a Wood Dimensional Door on a rift and step through.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_room_of_y: A Quartz Dimensional Door always leads to the same room, and nobody else can get in.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_out_of_ti: Set your spawn inside a pocket
Set your spawn inside your pocket room and that's where you'll wake up.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_shared_sp: An Iron Dimensional Door placed anywhere opens a new room that other players can wander into too.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_door_to_a: Gold, Stone and Amalgam doors lead into chains of dungeon rooms. Every door you take goes deeper, and the deeper rooms have better chests and much worse company.
task.integrated_boogaloo.rifts_limbo.des: Dying inside a pocket doesn't kill you. It drops you into Limbo, and something is waiting at the bottom.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_clo: A Viewfinder is a camera you can aim and look through. A Television only plays while it has a redstone signal and power wired from a generator with the Wrench.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_liv: Right-click a Viewfinder with a Hollow Cassette, then put the cassette in a TV to watch that camera live. It works with Viewfinders, not Security Cameras.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_big: Televisions placed side by side join into one big screen, up to eight blocks wide.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_dragon: A grown female drops an egg when you harvest her body. Nightmare eggs hatch standing in fire, Snow Wraith eggs in water and Skrill eggs out in the rain.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_take_c: A hatchling belongs to whoever placed the egg. The Command Staff, made from a dragon skull, tells it to sit, stand or follow you.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_light_: A Dragon Forge only runs while a dragon of the same element can see its core. A grown, tame Nadder or Gronckle told to sit nearby will work a fire forge, and a Night Fury a lightning one, at half the speed.
task.integrated_boogaloo.hit_list_dragon: Forge Adamantium with dragon blood to make dragonsteel. It goes into dragonsteel armor and swords.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.antarchy: Glowcap, Biowart, Moleworm, Wormy and Brooding Tunnel regions escalate differently. In most of them the last wave of a swarm brings a Hercules Beetle or a Hydra.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.witchery: Wolfsbane binds the Werewolf Altar. Belladonna Flowers turn up in poppets and in the Hydra rite.
A Fume Extension on each side of the oven, two at most, raises the chance of a catch.
What it catches
Heads, candelabras, a Chalice and a Pentacle on top raise its power. A Chalice is an Attuned Amethyst set in gold.
The Onyx Pedestal makes Attuned Onyx, for the Necromantic Stone, and Attuned Moonstone, for the Werewolf Altar and the Eternal Catalyst.
Focused Will and Condensed Fear, from a Brew of Flowing Spirit and Oil of Vitriol, feed the Brazier's summonings.
Rituals and Chalk
Drawing a circle

Every rite has Golden Chalk at the center and rings of chalk around it, and each rite has its own ring shape and size. Lay the ingredients inside, on the ground or on a Grassper, then right-click the Golden Chalk.

Rites draw on the Altar. Some only work by day, some at night and a few under a full moon. Ritual Chalk draws the plain rings. Golden Chalk is Mandrake Root, a gold nugget and Ritual Chalk stirred in the cauldron.
Some rites ask for colored rings of Infernal or Otherwhere Chalk, both stirred in the cauldron.
Pet rites bind a creature into a pet you carry. Each takes a Poppet, a few offerings and the creature standing in the circle.
A mob head and Vegetal in an Infernal Chalk ring bring that creature back. Potion Pendants are filled the same way.
Calling Viltrum
Rites that reach past the sky
Call of Viltrum brings Lucan, Vidor and Thula down to the circle half a minute after it's cast.
Challenge of Conquest calls Conquest. It only works at night and draws twice the altar power.
Viltrumite Bounty swaps the Attuned Stone for a Taglock and sends the three after whoever it's bound to.
None of them are heard outside the Overworld, and the offerings are wasted anywhere else. For the Bounty, it's the target who has to be there.
It makes Mutandis, the colored chalks, every brew, the teas, ciders and liquors, and Midnight Solution.
Custom potions start with a Nether Wart. Most effects use up capacity, so put the ingredients that add capacity in early.

The cauldron makes four at a time from Mandrake Root, Exhale of the Horned One and a Radium Shard. Stirred with a potion of Chemical X it becomes Mutandis Extremis, which the Hydra rite and the Drop of Luck need.

Every summoning starts with Wormwood. Add Condensed Fear and Ectoplasm for a Gravewailer, Pure Darkness and Focused Will for a Poltergeist, or a Vesper Wing and Ectoplasm for a Spectre. All three drop Ectoplasm.
Other mixes burn as incense instead. Graveyard Mist is gunpowder, Wood Ash and glowstone dust.

Brew of Revealing removes invisibility and shows spectral creatures. Brew of the Depths lets you breathe underwater but not in the air. Brew of Raising raises one of the dead, and Brew of the Grotesque makes villagers run from you.
Brew of Flowing Spirit can only be brewed in the Spirit World. Thrown, it leaves a pool that heals whoever stands in it. Thrown on a double door there, it opens a Spirit Portal.
The portal only lets you through after the Rite of Manifestation.
Level 10 takes the life of a villager or another player.
Up to five abilities can be active at once, chosen from what your level has unlocked, such as Wolf Form, Werewolf Form, Night Howl and Pack Summon.
Level 9 takes five villagers trapped in cages. For level 10, turn a villager: one handed a Wine Glass of your blood, with a Coffin nearby, becomes a vampire.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_c: Black powder comes from Onyx and white from Moonstone.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_p: Each structure's placer is crafted on the Pedestal around a spare Pedestal of the new tier.
The Complex placer needs Moonstone Chiseled Basalt, which only a finished Complex can make. Borrow it from the moonstone temples in the Forgotten Cities.
Polished Shellstone, Myrmite, Broodstone and Nyxite can replace polished basalt in all of these.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_b: Each bottle holds something alive. Placed next to its food, it spreads through it. Break what's left for the product.
Fading eats leaves, pumpkins, melons, hay, moss, dried kelp and mushroom blocks and leaves Vegetal. An empty bottle scoops it back up.
Failing eats obsidian, crying obsidian, Potent Nyxite and Chitin Blocks and leaves Neolith.
Ruin eats bedrock and leaves Bedrock Dust. Where it reaches the floor of the world, a Fissure opens into Imbrifer.
A Bottle of Decay Away, made from Neolith, Bluestone and green pigment, clears up all three.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_a: Drop an anvil onto items lying on the ground and it crushes them. Gem shards and buds turn into Gemstone Powder, and colored leaves give up Pigment.
It also breaks blocks down a step at a time, from stone to cobblestone to gravel to sand. Iron and diamond buds crush into ingots and diamonds.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_t: The Titration Barrel ferments drinks. Every recipe has a minimum wait, and the longer you leave it past that, the stronger the drink.
The clock runs in real hours, so the barrel keeps working while the game is closed. Barrels in hot biomes lose more of the batch as it ages.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.starlit_: The Starlit Factory forges the celestial weapons and Lunar Stone armor. Mjölnir, Stormbreaker and the Infinity Gauntlet are put together here too.
It runs on Stardust, loose or in blocks. Long recipes burn through a lot of it, so fill it up before you start.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_f: Later fusions use Liquid Crystal or Midnight Solution in place of lava.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_l: The Enchanter's structure needs four buckets of it. The Perfect Compound and the Mysterious Locket are both fused in a Shrine filled with it.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_i: Someone built those cities and then left. If you find writing down there, I'd like to read it.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cave_aby: The Hullbreaker hunts anything that glows, so put your lights out when it starts circling. It drops the Immortal Embryo that Big Bertha's handle needs.
Abyssal Ruins hold Diving Suit pieces, and sometimes a broken Submarine you can fix with copper ingots. Bring water breathing.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cave_can: The Gum Worm drops the Sweet Tooth that Big Bertha's hilt needs. Candicorns can be tamed with Caramel Apples and ridden with a saddle. Feed a Gummy Bear a potion and when it wakes from its long sleep it sheds Jelly Beans with that potion's effect.
Caniacs sometimes drop a Sharpened Candy Cane, which makes a Candy Cane Hook for swinging across the gaps.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cave_for: When Underzealots catch a Gloomoth, their ritual turns it into a Watcher. It stalks you and freezes you in place to look through its eyes. If they catch a Vesper they make a Forsaken instead, which has 250 health and heals in the dark.
The Forsaken drops the Pure Darkness that Big Bertha's blade needs. Watchers can drop an Occult Gem. Bring a shield and a lot of torches.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cave_mag: Boundroids drop the Heavyweight that Big Bertha's blade needs. Teletors drop neodymium and a Telecore, which makes a Galena Gauntlet. Magnetrons leave a Heart of Iron.
Neodymium Ingots make magnets and Seeking Arrows.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cave_pri: To tame a Tremorsaurus, stun it with a Primitive Club and feed it Serene Salad, over and over. Tame two and breed them with Dinosaur Chops to get the egg Big Bertha's hilt needs.
Throw an Ominous Catalyst into a volcano to wake the Luxtructosaurus. Atlatitans only appear once it's dead.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cave_tox: Raycats are harmless. Tame one with Radgill, the fish in the acid, and it keeps Nucleepers away and soaks up your radiation.
Uranium is common in the walls. A Raygun is built from what you find here, and Big Bertha's handle needs one. Bring Hazmat Armor, which cuts down radiation and acid.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.stone_mi: Command: look at a creature up to 48 blocks away and it obeys you for 15 seconds. It goes after whatever you last hit or whatever last hit you, and otherwise the nearest thing it can fight. A player can be steered. You wait 15 seconds between uses.
Mind Sight: a creature you look at glows for 15 seconds and you see its health and armor. Look at nothing and everything within 32 blocks glows. 10 second wait.
Mind Beam: hold to charge for up to two seconds, then let go. A full charge reaches 64 blocks and hits hardest.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.stone_ti: Chronostasis: hold it and everything else in that world stops, other players included, until you let go.
Temporal Dilation: look at a creature and slow it to a twentieth of its speed, or speed it up to three times normal. It hangs in the air while you adjust it.

Time Field: everything within 20 blocks of the spot you're looking at runs at a quarter speed for 20 seconds, then there's a 30 second wait. Crouch when you use it and the whole world you're in slows down instead, with a one minute wait.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.stone_sp: Space Fold: look at a block up to 320 blocks away and you're standing next to it. 5 second wait.

Dimensional Rift: pick a destination first. It can be any world and any coordinates, or a world nobody has been to yet. Then look at a surface within 32 blocks to open a rift there. It works both ways and stays open for a minute. Crouch when you use it to go straight there without a rift.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.stone_po: Strength Surge: Strength X for 20 seconds. It's ready again as soon as it wears off.
Annihilation Beam: hold to charge for up to two seconds, then let go. It tears through the ground and anything standing in the way, out to 64 blocks at full charge.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.stone_so: Soul Exchange: take up to five hearts from a creature you're looking at and heal by that much. Crouch to give it up to five of yours instead. 5 second wait.
Soul Sever: a creature freezes for 8 seconds, and nothing can hurt it until it thaws. 12 second wait.

Reap and Restore: while this power is chosen, anything that dies within 32 blocks of you, you included, hangs on for 5 seconds. Use it on the remnant to bring it back with about a third of its health. Crouch and use it on a living creature to kill it. 10 second wait.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.stone_re: Reality Rewrite: a block you look at, up to 24 blocks away, turns to stone, then amethyst, gold, diamond, emerald, obsidian and bedrock each time you use it. It changes back after 10 seconds. Chests, furnaces and other blocks that hold things can't be changed.
Gravity Inversion: a creature you look at falls upward for 15 seconds.
Size Shift: change a creature's size, anywhere from a hundredth to a hundred times normal. This one doesn't wear off.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.infinity: Every Stone works the same in both. Only the Infinity Gauntlet does more with all six: it adds the Infinity Beam and the Snap.
The Snap ends a random half of every living thing in every loaded world. You and whatever you're riding are spared. Other players are not. It only goes off if you use it twice within five seconds.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_drag: Monstrous Nightmares nest in deserts, jungles, badlands, savannas, plains and high peaks and breathe fire. Snow Wraiths live in snowy country and freeze you in place. Skrills take swamps, jungles, badlands and savannas and breathe lightning. None nest within about a thousand blocks of where the world began.
An egg hatches after about six minutes in the right spot, and the hatchling is tame to whoever placed it.
Two dragons of one breed, both 75 days or older, breed on their lily mixture, and the female lays in a nest. Each lily grows where its breed nests.
Dragons age a day for every day that passes. Dragon Meal adds one on the spot, and Sickly Dragon Meal stops growth until the next Dragon Meal.
A dead dragon leaves its body behind, and each click takes one thing from it. An older dragon has more to give.
A female 75 days or older drops an egg with the heart. The skull comes last.
Scale armor cuts the damage from dragon breath. Dragon bone weapons also need Witherbones, which wither skeletons and cockatrices drop.

A tame or chained dragon of the same element breathes into the Dragon Forge's Aperture. A grown, tame Nadder or Gronckle within ten blocks works a fire forge and a Night Fury a lightning one, at half speed.
The forge makes blood from scales, and dragonsteel from an Adamantium Ingot and blood. Dragonsteel goes into armor, swords, and Mjölnir, Stormbreaker, Solaris and Frostbound at the Starlit Factory.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_tame: A Summoning Crystal made with its breed's blood binds to a dragon and calls it to you. From 50 days old you can brush a few scales off your own dragon, and each Dragon Meal lets you brush once more.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_scri: Manuscripts turn up in dragon roosts, dragon caves and mausoleums. Three of them make a Bestiary, a picture book of the creatures out there.
Put the Bestiary in a Bestiary Lectern with spare manuscripts and pick from the pages it offers. A villager who claims the Lectern becomes a Scribe and trades manuscripts for emeralds and back.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_cycl: It drops leather, mutton and wool. Kill it yourself for the Eye of Cyclops, which weakens every hostile mob near you while you hold it. Big Bertha's handle needs one.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_trol: Troll Leather makes armor that cuts projectile damage, by 70 percent for a full set. Tusks go into the Bonking book at the Enchanter, or grind down into bone meal.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_cock: It drops feathers, chicken and Witherbones, which dragon bone weapons need. Kill one yourself for a chance at the rare Cockatrice Eye. It makes the Cockatrice Scepter, which withers several targets at once, and the Puncturing book.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_amph: Its feathers make Amphithere Arrows, which knock mobs back, the Amphithere Macuahuitl, which knocks targets up and disables shields, and Breezebreaker at the Starlit Factory.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_sea_: Fangs and scales together make Tide Arrows and the Tide Trident. A fang also goes into Big Bertha's handle, Aquaflora at the Starlit Factory and the Tsunami book.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_hipp: It drops feathers and leather. Kill one yourself for a chance at a Hippogryph Talon, which makes the Hippogryph Talon Sword. Every swing of that sword sweeps.
It drops Shiny Scales. Kill one yourself for a chance at a Hippocampus Fin, which makes the Hippocampus Slapper and the Sea Swing book. The Slapper dazes and slows whatever it hits.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_sire: She drops prismarine and Shiny Scales. Kill one yourself for a chance at a Siren Tear, used in the Gorgon rite, the Siren Flute, Rainfall Serenity and the Seapairing book. The flute makes mobs fall in love for ten seconds, and they can't attack while it lasts.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_ghos: Ghosts drop Ectoplasm. Kill one yourself for a chance at a Phantasmal Ingot. Added to a Dragon Bone Sword it makes the Phantasmal Blade, which throws spinning swords that pass through walls. It's also the core of Poltergeist at the Starlit Factory.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.iaf_pixi: Pixie Dust goes into Crescentia and the Lunar Stone armor at the Starlit Factory. Kill a pixie yourself for a chance at Pixie Wings, which make the Pixie Wand. The wand uses dust as ammo and leaves its targets floating.
task.integrated_boogaloo.boogaloo_rainbo: Regular sugar does nothing for a Rainbow Ant, it has to be Rainbow Sugar. You make it on an Onyx Pedestal out of sugar, six pigments, a uranium nugget and some corn syrup, and it comes out two at a time. Antazon sells a few a day if you can't wait that long!
task.integrated_boogaloo.boogaloo_ultima: Titanium and Uranium from Cavaryn make Ultimate armor, the best metal you can wear. Get the whole set and hang on to it. Bedrock armor and both kinds of royal armor are built on top of these pieces.
Collect a full set of Ultimate armor
task.integrated_boogaloo.boogaloo_bedroc: Put each Ultimate piece in a Fusion Shrine filled with Midnight Solution, along with Bedrock Dust, black pigment, onyx powder and a Block of Uranium. The dust is the hard part. You get it by breaking the decayed bedrock deep down with a Bottle of Ruin, and A World of Color walks you there. Bedrock tools are made the same way. Sneak and use a Bedrock pickaxe, axe, shovel or hoe to switch it between 1x1, 3x3 and 5x5 mining. The pickaxe and axe have one more setting that breaks every connected block of the same kind.
Wear a full set of Bedrock Armor
task.integrated_boogaloo.boogaloo_royal_: The King dropped more than the Mind Stone. Eight King Scales around an Ultimate piece turn it into Royal Guardian armor. With the chestplate on, G raises a Royal Boundary that stops arrows in midair and gives your friends Strength. The sword switches between fire, frost and storm, and the shield gets nearby creatures fighting on your side.

Queen Scales do the same thing for the Royal Assailant set, eight around each Ultimate piece. R in the chestplate flips your gravity so you can walk on the ceiling, and the boots mean falling up doesn't hurt. The Battle Axe opens black holes and the Staff calls in four Manticores. Her whole family fights with gravity, apparently.
task.integrated_boogaloo.engineering_veh: A new car can't go anywhere yet. Wheels come from a Wheel Bench and seats from a Seat Bench. Hold a part near the car and a green outline shows where it fits, then right-click there. A red outline means it's the wrong size. Hit a part with the Wrench to take it back off, or sneak and hit the car with it to pick the whole thing up.
task.integrated_boogaloo.engineering_fue:
Engines need fuel, and lava works in every one of them. Refinery fuel and diesel work too. Put a Fuel Pump down next to the car, fill it with buckets or pipe fuel into the bottom, then click the pump and it hooks onto the nearest vehicle by itself. A Jerrycan is for the car you left out of gas somewhere.

Once you're in, W, S, A and D drive, and U opens the panel with the engine switch and the lights.
task.integrated_boogaloo.engineering_loc: Right now anyone can hop in and drive off. Right-click your car with a Key to tie the key to it and lock it. After that only someone holding that key can get in, and only you can swap its parts. Craft a key on its own to wipe it.
task.integrated_boogaloo.engineering_tak: Planes and helicopters get built the same way, and propellers come from a Propeller Bench. Flying is harder though. I and K set the throttle, W and S pitch, A and D roll, J and L turn the rudder and B brakes. Read the Plane Handbook before you take one up. I didn't, and I'd rather not talk about it.
task.integrated_boogaloo.start_here_kitc: Pies, cobblers, sushi, pizza and most other proper meals don't come from a crafting table. You build them on a Cutting Board, one ingredient at a time and in the right order. A Frying Pan on a Stove, the Oven, the Toaster and the Microwave cook the rest. Those need power, so link them to a generator with the Wrench.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.controls: These are the starting keys. You can change any of them in Options, under Controls.

§ePowers and suits:§r R, G, V, C and X are abilities one to five. Iron Man suits use R and G. H takes the helmet off and Shift+H calls the suit to you. Holding the key for a power with a wheel lets you switch its passives.
§eMorph:§r Alt with the same five keys. [ and ] pick the form.
§eInfinity Gauntlet:§r hold it, then Left and Right pick a Stone and Up and Down pick its power. O sets where the Space Stone sends you.
§eArmor:§r R flips your gravity in Royal Assailant armor and hides you in Tiger's Eye armor. G raises the Royal Boundary in Royal Guardian armor.
§eRiding:§r R breathes fire or toggles flight, G is the special attack and X brings you down. Left Ctrl charges.
§eGuns:§r R reloads and Shift+R unloads. K is a melee hit, J swaps ammo, Z opens attachments and X inspects.
§eVehicles:§r W, S, A and D drive, and U opens the panel for the engine and lights.
§eEverything else:§r B opens your backpack, Y the witchcraft wheel, Left Alt is the witchcraft utility key, I opens implants, ; opens your accessories and M the map.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.falls_shi: A miner's shift log. The last page is the same as the first.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.falls_not: A typed-up notice from a village board. Somebody kept adding to it.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.falls_fri: Notes taken off a fridge and typed up in the order they were stuck on.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.falls_unl: No label. It's warm, and it's getting warmer.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.falls_cli: Four notches cut into the label. Something inside is scratching to get out.
task.integrated_boogaloo.engineering_tar: Build a console, then use Hull Glue to attach a small hull. Titanium and Time Steel make the frame.
Make a TARDIS Matrix in the Oritech Assembler. Fit it to the console to claim the ship as your own.
Fit a Fluid Link and an Artron Cell, then charge the console. The Artron Generator burns coal and charcoal.
Fit the Dematerialisation Circuit for vortex travel. Add the helm, throttle, navigation computer, flight stabilisers and time rotor.
Fit a Dimensional Stabiliser for travel between dimensions
Build the Architectural Reconfiguration Rig around your ship to turn it into a police box. Charge the rig before converting it.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.tardis.b: The console and its upgrades take titanium, Time Steel, blood crystals and machine parts. The TARDIS Matrix comes out of the Assembler.
Place a Junk TARDIS Console, use Hull Glue to attach a small hull, then fit the Matrix, Fluid Link and Artron Cell. A generator burning coal or charcoal, conduits and capacitors supply artron power.
Fit the helm, throttle, navigation computer, flight stabilisers, time rotor and Dematerialisation Circuit before your first trip. A Dimensional Stabiliser opens up other dimensions.

Memory Banks save destinations and Navigation Calibrators land you closer. The Architectural Reconfiguration Rig, a Rig Controller and four Rig Pylons on artron power, turns the ship into a police box with a bigger inside.
computer.integrated_boogaloo.product.mat: Sixteen Topaz Shards for your next batch of colorwork.
Sixteen Citrine Shards, sorted and ready for the Pedestal.
Sixteen Amethyst Shards without another trip underground.
Eight Onyx Shards without waiting for midnight.
Four Polished Onyx blocks for building or unpacking into thirty-six shards.
Eight Moonstone Shards for work that needs a little more light.
Four fragrant Nightdew Sprouts for brewing and cultivation.
An exceptionally rare Nightdew bloom with powerful sleep magic. One bloom per order.
Sixteen Vegetal for growing things and further experiments.
Eight Neolith without sacrificing another pile of obsidian.
Eight Midnight Chips for your next experiment.
Four Star Fragments without spending another night watching the sky.
task.integrated_boogaloo.pastel_nightdew: Find a Nightdew Sprout; a Sniffer can uncover one. Antazon then stocks sprout refills and rare Nectardew Burgeons, and buys your surplus.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_be: Implants are crafted on the bench's 5 by 5 grid. Nearly all of them are built from the same dozen components plus titanium.
It can also take an implant apart for some of its components. Scavenged cyberware breaks down the same way.
An implant does nothing until it's installed at a Surgery Table or a Robosurgeon.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_gr: The Grafting Table joins body parts into wetware, implants made from flesh. Lungs and a Gyroscopic Bladder become an Aerostatic Gyrobladder, and a Heart with echo shards and a sculk catalyst becomes a Sculk Heart.
Many of the parts drop from mobs. Wetware is installed like any other implant.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_cp:
AUTHOR: DR. SELENE MARROW, NEURODIGITAL CONTINUITY DIVISION
DOCUMENT STATUS: INTERNAL REVIEW COPY

The Cerebral Processing Unit (CPU) represents the first successful artificial substrate capable of sustaining a digitized human consciousness outside of its original biological brain. This paper summarizes the creation, calibration, failure cases, and safe implementation requirements of CPU-based consciousness transplantation.

Early public-facing descriptions of the technology have been dangerously simplistic. The Cerebral Processing Unit is not a replacement “brain” in the conventional sense. It is an artificial neuro-computational organ designed to run a Digital Human Freight (DHF) file, hereafter referred to as a DHF.

Without a valid DHF, the unit is empty hardware.
With the wrong DHF, the unit is lethal.
With the correct DHF, the subject survives.

Survival, however, should not be mistaken for permanence.

I. ARTIFICIAL LOBE CONSTRUCTION

A functional Cerebral Processing Unit must be assembled from individually fabricated artificial lobes. These lobes serve as specialized processing structures modeled after broad functional regions of the human brain.

Early prototypes using a single unified processor failed consistently. The human mind does not respond well to undifferentiated computation. Memory, motor intention, sensory interpretation, emotional regulation, and identity continuity require separated but synchronized quantum processing architecture.

The lobe-based model proved significantly more stable. Each artificial lobe contributes to the final unit’s ability to preserve a subject’s continuity of self after biological transfer.

The completed Cerebral Processing Unit should be considered inert until paired with a valid DHF file. A blank unit contains no personality, memory, continuity thread, or self-recognition map.

It is not dormant. It is empty.

II. BIOCHIP RECORDING PERIOD

The DHF cannot be created instantly.

To generate a viable Digital Human Freight file, the subject must first install a biochip into a Chipware Slot and maintain continuous use for a full twenty-eight day observation period.

This period allows the biochip to record long-form neural patterning, memory indexing habits, emotional response curves, motor intention signatures, dream-state drift, stress behavior, and self-identification anchors.

The duration is not arbitrary.

Shorter recordings produced convincing but unstable copies. Subjects with incomplete DHF files demonstrated speech continuity and memory recall for several minutes after transplantation, followed by severe disorientation, motor collapse, identity fracture, or total shutdown.

In one case, a subject with a thirteen-day DHF recognized their own name, answered three personal questions correctly, then began asking why their hands belonged to “the other one.”

Removal of the biochip during the recording period resets the process. This is not merely a data-loss issue. Discontinuous recordings produce pattern mismatches that cannot be reliably repaired. A broken continuity thread is worse than an incomplete one, because the resulting DHF may appear viable during preliminary validation while still failing during live transplantation.
The biochip must remain installed. The recording must complete. There are no safe shortcuts.

III. DHF INTEGRATION INTO THE CPU

Once a complete DHF has been recorded, the file must be physically and computationally integrated into the Cerebral Processing Unit using a Netherite Quantum Processor.

The quantum processor appears to serve two critical functions.

First, it binds the DHF to the processing architecture of the CPU without flattening its self-referential data structures.

Second, it stabilizes the identity-checking process required during implantation.

The DHF must belong to the recipient.

This cannot be overstated.

A Cerebral Processing Unit loaded with no DHF results in immediate subject death upon installation. There is no mind present for the body to reconnect to. The nervous system attempts to resolve against an empty cognitive substrate and fails catastrophically.

A Cerebral Processing Unit loaded with another person’s DHF is also fatal. The body rejects the identity mismatch at every level: neurological, cybernetic, and metaphysical, if one is inclined toward less precise language. In practical terms, the subject dies before either identity can establish stable control.

The popular claim that a DHF can be used to “overwrite” another person is unsupported by all controlled results. The body does not become the donor. The donor does not survive through the recipient. Both patterns collapse.

The only viable pairing is:

Subject A records DHF.
Subject A loads DHF into CPU.
Subject A receives CPU.

Any deviation from this chain has resulted in death.

IV. TRANSPLANTATION OUTCOME

Successful transplantation replaces the subject’s biological brain with the Cerebral Processing Unit while preserving sufficient continuity for the subject to awaken, recognize themselves, and resume function.

Subjects commonly report the following within the first hour:

A sensation of internal silence.
Reduced emotional immediacy.
Heightened clarity of memory access.
Difficulty distinguishing remembered sensation from current sensory input.
Temporary uncertainty regarding breathing, blinking, or heartbeat expectation.
Phantom pressure in the skull.

These effects typically stabilize within the first day.

More concerning is the immediate disappearance of the Humanity index.

After successful CPU transplantation, Humanity is no longer the relevant measure of psychological strain. Additional cyberware does not degrade the subject in the same way it does in biologically brained individuals.

Instead, we've developed a new stability metric for gauging the neurological health of the subject: Data Integrity.

V. DATA INTEGRITY DEGRADATION

Data Integrity represents the current health of both the DHF and the operating system sustaining it.

Unlike Humanity, Data Integrity is not reduced by installing implants. The transplanted subject can tolerate cybernetic expansion without the same biological rejection of identity produced in standard subjects.

This advantage led to reckless early claims that CPU recipients were immune to cyberpsychosis.

They are not. They simply fail by a different mechanism.

The digitized mind is not static. It continues to think, learn, remember, associate, dream, misremember, react, and reinterpret itself. Every new input is processed through the DHF. Every processed input slightly rewrites the conditions by which the next input will be interpreted.

In biological tissue, this recursive instability is dampened by organic repair, sleep architecture, chemical regulation, and the imprecise mercy of forgetting. In a CPU, the process is exact, and infectious to the rest of the system. One scientist has likened it's spread to that of prion diseases, an analogy found suitable for understanding the problem.

The prevailing model compares DHF degradation to recursive artificial-data contamination: a copy learning from a copy learning from a copy, each generation introducing slight distortions until the original pattern remains recognizable only in outline.

A human mind running on artificial substrate gradually consumes its own outputs. It learns from its own interpretations. It references reconstructed memories of reconstructed memories. It experiences the world, compresses the world, reintegrates the compression, then uses that reintegration as the next layer of self.

Over time, this becomes caustic, not only to the DHF, but to the operating system responsible for maintaining it.

Most subjects reach critical instability after approximately seven days without restoration. The exact rate varies by stress exposure, implant load, sensory intensity, sleep deprivation, combat activity, and emotional trauma. The pattern is consistent.

VI. DATA INTEGRITY RESTORATION PROTOCOL

The Data Integrity Restoration Protocol was developed after the first long-duration CPU subjects began exhibiting cyberpsychotic symptoms despite stable implant compatibility.

Initial assumptions blamed hardware overheating, power instability, hostile network intrusion, or DHF transcription error. These explanations accounted for individual cases, but not the broader pattern.

The breakthrough came after Subject 18 entered a spontaneous low-activity state resembling sleep. During this state, corrupted associative chains decreased, missing reference paths were rebuilt, and personality drift partially reversed.

Modern Cerebral Processing Units now include this built-in Data Integrity Restoration Protocol that launches during sleep/reboot cycles. The protocol scans both the DHF and the operating environment, identifies corrupted or broken cognitive files, reconstructs missing pattern links, clears unstable feedback loops, and restores damaged continuity anchors where possible.

CPU recipients must sleep semi-regularly to prevent Data Integrity collapse. The subject may not feel tired in the traditional biological sense, but the absence of fatigue should not be interpreted as safety.

VII. FAILURE SYMPTOMS

When Data Integrity falls below safe thresholds, symptoms resemble cyberpsychosis but differ in origin.

At moderate degradation, subjects report visual distortions, auditory artifacts, emotional flattening, memory echoes, and brief episodes of self-observation, often described as “watching someone else use your body.”

At severe degradation, subjects experience intrusive violent logic, derealization, fragmented identity loops, and inability to distinguish present threats from remembered or simulated ones.

At catastrophic degradation, the subject may enter fugue behavior. These episodes are characterized by partial or total loss of self-directed control, violent threat classification errors, and extreme difficulty restoring baseline cognition without external intervention.

The subject becomes unstable because the digital structure carrying the mind has begun to collapse.

VIII. SAFE IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Based on all recorded trials, safe implementation of CPU consciousness transplantation requires the following:

The Cerebral Processing Unit must be assembled from complete artificial lobes.
The subject must maintain a biochip in chipware storage for the full twenty-eight day recording period.
The biochip must not be removed before recording completion.
The completed DHF must be integrated into the CPU using a Netherite Quantum Processor.
The DHF must belong to the same subject receiving the CPU.
Blank CPUs must never be installed.
Foreign-DHF CPUs must never be installed.
Post-transplant subjects must treat sleep as mandatory system maintenance, regardless of perceived fatigue.
Data Integrity must be monitored as aggressively as cardiac function, oxygenation, or energy reserves.

IX. CONCLUSION

The Cerebral Processing Unit is not immortality. It is not resurrection. It is not a clean escape from the limits of the human body. It is a controlled relocation of consciousness from biological tissue into artificial architecture, dependent on correct recording, correct identity matching, and continuous file maintenance.

While the procedure can save a life, it can also end one instantly. The distinction lies almost entirely in preparation.

A completed CPU without a DHF is a coffin.
A completed CPU with the wrong DHF is an execution device.
A completed CPU with a properly recorded, properly integrated, self-matched DHF is a viable artificial brain.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_ol:
FILE STATUS: CORRUPTED / PARTIAL
SPEAKER: UNKNOWN MALE, ESTIMATED AGE 50–60

[BEGIN TRANSCRIPT]

It started with an Arm Cannon. That was the first one. First real piece of chrome they bolted into me when I signed the papers. “Mandatory battlefield integration,” they called it. Like I had the option to say no. Not that I would’ve.

I was twenty-one. Dumb as gravel and twice as easy to kick around. No eddies. No family worth calling. Just a pair of hands, a bad attitude, and this stupid dream that if I wore the right uniform and killed the right people, I’d come home as somebody folks respected.

Funny thing, ain’t it? They don’t sell you the war. Not really. They sell you the man you think you’ll be after. Strong. Useful. Honored. Honor. F********* HONOR.

WHAT DO THEY KNOW ABOUT HONOR? THEY PIN IT ON YOU AFTER THEY TEACH YOU WHERE TO AIM. THEY TEACH YOU THE SOFT PLACES. THEY TEACH YOU HOW FAST A BODY OPENS WHEN THE CANNON SPINS HOT. THE ENEMY SPILLING OUT OF THEMSELVES. THEN THEY SHAKE YOUR HAND. THEN THEY LOOK AWAY. LOOK AT ME. LOOK AT WHAT YOU BOUGHT. LOOK AT WHAT YOU—

[BREATHING SHIFTS]

Sorry. Thought I had more time before that started...

[BREATHING RELAXES]

They said the Arm Cannon would keep me alive. Said the targeting module would make me sharp. Said the reinforced skeleton was an investment in survivability. Said the Neural Processor would help me handle battlefield stress.

Battlefield stress. That’s corpo talk for remembering the sound a man makes when half of him is gone and the other half hasn’t figured it out yet.

I was good, though. I’ll say that much. I was damn good. Not brave. Don’t let anybody sell you that braindance garbage. Bravery is what they call it after, when some kid in a clean shirt writes your name on a wall. Out there, it was fear. Fear and orders. Fear and mud. Fear and the little lights in your optic display telling you the cannon was ready to fire again.

I fired when they told me.

Again.

And again.

And again.

Again.

Funny how a word gets stuck.

Again.

The light went green.

Again.

Orders came down.

Again.

Somebody ran.

Again.

Somebody screamed.

Again.

I got medals for that sh**. Little squares of metal for making people into shredded synthmeat.

[LONG PAUSE]

When I came back, they shook my hand with the one I still had.

Said I was a credit to the program. Said my service would never be forgotten. Said there were transition benefits, clinic vouchers, priority housing, employment placement, mental wellness support.

You ever hear a lie so pretty you almost thank the bastard for it?

Priority housing meant a cot in a veteran stack with black mold in the vents. Employment placement meant bouncing outside clubs for kids who’d never seen a gunshot but dressed like they survived a massacre. Clinic vouchers meant the cheap docs would look at my chrome, whistle through their teeth, and say, “That’s military proprietary. Can’t touch it, choom.”

Choom. I hate that word now.

Everybody’s your choom till your parts start failing.

Choom, choom, choom.

They say it soft when they want something. Say it friendly. Like a leash with a smile on it. Choom, hold this door. Choom, take this job. Choom, watch my back. Choom, bleed over there where I don’t have to see it.

You're not my choom.

[LOW LAUGHTER]

I should’ve charged more. Should’ve charged by the scar.

The Arm Cannon was first to go twitchy. Misfires. Phantom charge cycles. Sometimes I’d wake up with it humming hot against my skin like it wanted something. Like it missed the old days.

Then the legs. Standard issue cyberlegs, Linear Frame reinforcement, with cheap actuators under expensive branding. Fine for sprinting across kill zones. Not so fine for sleeping under overpasses in winter.

Cold gets in the joints. You know that? Nobody tells you that. Cold gets in the joints and stays there. Makes every step sound like a door opening in an empty house.

I did merc work because what else was I gonna do? Sit in a support group and talk about feelings while my battery indicator blinked red? I knew violence. Violence still paid. Not well, not steady, but enough.

At first, the young ones respected me. Called me "Old Dog". Called me "Sir" sometimes. I liked that more than I should’ve.

Then they started getting faster.

New mercs. Fresh faces. Designer chrome. Mantis blades. Sandevistans. Threat Matrixes. Eye modules that could count the teeth in your skull from across the street. Borged out beyond your wildest dreams. They’d slide into fixer booths all shiny and starving, talking loud about contracts they hadn’t earned yet.

And me? I was the relic in the corner with a jammed cannon and a bad knee.

Relic.

That’s a word for something dead that people still charge eddies to look at.

I could feel them measuring me. Could feel their optics sliding over the dents. Over the old ports. Over the mismatched plating. They’d look at my arm first. Always the arm. Then the face. Then the boots.

Boots tell you a lot.

Mine said I’d been walking too long.

So I upgraded. Just a little.

Pneumatic Wrists first. Helped with recoil. Helped me reload faster. Helped me punch through armor when somebody got too close.

Then Reinforced Knuckles. Because everybody needs a backup.

Then a Targeting Module, because my hands shook when it rained and I got tired of pretending they didn’t.

Then Bonelacing. Then a Dense Battery. Then the Sandevistan.

Should’ve stopped there.

I know that. I knew it then, too.

But you gotta understand something. When the world throws you away, and then some back-alley ripper says, “I can make you useful again,” that doesn’t sound like temptation.

It sounds like mercy.

[STATIC]

Mercy.

MERCY IS A HOOK. MERCY IS THE LINE THEY PUT THROUGH YOUR JAW. THEY PULL AND YOU DANCE. YOU DANCE AND YOU BLEED AND THEY CLAP. I’LL MAKE THEM CLAP. I’LL MAKE THEM PUT THEIR HANDS TOGETHER. I’LL TAKE THE HANDS. I’LL TAKE THE ARMS. I’LL OPEN THEM UP AND SHOW THEM WHAT THEY BOUGHT—

[HEAVY BREATHING]

No, that’s not... Stop.

That’s not where I was. Where was I?

The Sandevistan. First time I triggered it, I cried. Ain’t ashamed to say it.

Whole world slowed down. Rain hanging in the air like glass beads. Muzzle flashes blooming soft and quiet. Some punk’s blade coming at my throat so slow I could’ve kissed it.

For one second, I was young again.

Not twenty-one young. Before that. Before the enlistment center. Before the posters. Before the recruiter with the white teeth and the handshake too firm to trust.

I was a kid running through wheat behind my mother’s house, fast enough to believe the whole world was behind me and none of it could catch up.

Then the implant cycle ended.

And I was an old man in an alley with three dead gonks around me and blood in my mouth that wasn’t mine. That’s when I knew I was getting fried.

Didn’t stop, though. Course I didn’t stop. Nobody stops. You think a man stops digging because he sees the hole?

No. He says, “Little deeper and maybe I’ll find daylight.”

So I sold the medals. Sold the jacket. Sold the last photo of my unit, which is funny, because I spent twenty years trying to forget those faces and cried like a child when the pawnbroker took them.

Shouldn’t have sold that photo. Stupid thing to miss. Faces on cheap paper. Half of them bastards. Half of them boys. Most of them dead.

There was one, Ortiz. He used to hum when he cleaned his rifle. Drove me mad. Same four notes. Over and over.

I can hear it sometimes.

[HUMMING]

Then screaming. Then the cannon.

Then silence.

Then four notes again.

[PAUSE]

If Ortiz is in there somewhere, I’m sorry, brother. If he isn’t, then I’m apologizing to static. That’s about right.

Got a Neural Contextualizer after that. Tool selection, combat assistance, reflexive decision support. Real clean piece of tech. Too clean for me.

It started choosing the cannon before I knew I was angry.

Some drunk bumped me outside a noodle stand, and my arm opened up, my optics lighting him up as a threat, all because some algorithm in my skull decided a scared man with soup on his shirt was a threat.

And I just laughed. He pissed himself and I laughed. I couldn't even help myself. Not because it was funny. It wasn’t. It was ugly. He was just some poor bastard trying to get home.

I still don't know why I laughed. It was like my implants had taken the wheel of my body, and I was tied up in the trunk.
Then screaming. So much screaming.
When I finally came to, I was covered in blood, hiding behind some back-alley dumpster.

[PAUSE]

That’s sick, ain’t it? But it’s true.

People walk through the poor like smoke unless they think the smoke can bite.

Then suddenly they see you. Then suddenly they remember manners. Then suddenly it’s sir, please, no trouble, I didn’t mean nothing.

I DIDN’T MEAN NOTHING. NOBODY EVER MEANS NOTHING. THEY BUMP YOU. THEY STEP OVER YOU. THEY TAKE YOUR YEARS, YOUR BLOOD, YOUR ARM, YOUR SLEEP, YOUR NAME. I’LL MAKE THEM NOTHING. I’LL—

[METAL SCRAPING]

[STATIC]

You lose things by inches.

People think cyberpsychosis is a switch. One day you’re a man, next day you’re a monster. That’s clean. People like clean.

It ain’t clean.

First you stop sleeping. Then food tastes like wet paper. Then music gets sharp. Lights get loud. Somebody coughs three tables over and your whole body inventories every way to kill them before you can blink.

Then come the voices.

Not voices like in the BDs. Nobody whispering your name from a vent. Nothing dramatic. It’s your voice, only meaner. Faster. Hungrier. The part of you that says, “walk away,” gets quieter. The part that says, “break his jaw before he reaches,” gets real persuasive.

Break.

That word gets stuck too.

Break the weapon. Break the line. Break the door. Break the jaw. Break the bones. Break the kid before the kid breaks you. Break first. Break fast. Break clean. BREAK THE SPINE. RIP IT OUT OF THE DUMB F***. MAKE HIM EAT THE CUR—

[SHARP EXHALE]

Sorry.

I tried Neuropozyne. When I could get it. Little yellowish mercy in a vial. Took the edge off. Made my hands feel like hands again for a while. But that stuff costs more than food, and food was already losing the argument.

Fixer told me to retire.

Retire.

Where? To what?

A cardboard box with a charging cable? A veteran shelter where they pat you down for weapons and then look surprised when the weapons are under your skin?

I told him I could still work.

He said, “You’re unstable.”

Unstable.

That’s what they call you when the thing they built starts making noise.

UNSTABLE. UNSTABLE. I’LL SHOW YOU UNSTABLE. I HELD THE LINE WHILE THEY HID IN TOWERS. I BURNED FOR THEM. I BLED OUT IN DITCHES FOR STOCK OPTIONS AND BOARDROOM MAPS. OPEN THE DOORS. OPEN THEIR CHESTS. LET ME SEE THE WIRES. LET ME PULL UNTIL THE SCREAMING—

[IMPACT NOISE]

Sorry.

Dropped the recorder. Hands aren’t so good tonight.

Funny. After all this chrome, after all the eddies and scars and backroom installs, the hands are still what give me away. They shake when I’m sad.

Not angry. Sad.

Anger steadies me. That scares me more than anything.

There was a girl once. Before the war. Alaina. She had this laugh, loud and mean, like she was daring the world to tell her to quiet down. I told her I’d come back with enough money to buy us a place near the river.

She said she didn’t want money.

I thought that meant she didn’t believe in me. Took me thirty years to figure out she meant she wanted me. Just me.

No cannon. No medals. No chrome. No blood under the nails.

I wonder if she’d recognize me now.

No. That’s a stupid thought. Course she wouldn’t.

I don’t recognize me.

[LONG STATIC BREAK]

There’s a kid been following my contracts. Calls himself Razor-Saint. Dumba** name. Nice jacket, though. New mantis blades, gold plated. Moves like he thinks death is something that happens to slower people.

He looked at me yesterday and smiled.

Not cruel, exactly.

Worse. Polite.

Young merc polite. The kind that says, “Move aside, old man. Your century is over.”

Can’t stop thinking about that.

Not the fancy blades. Not the tailored jacket. The smile.

Like he’d already buried me and was being respectful at the grave.

I wanted to warn him.

I wanted to tell him the city doesn’t make legends. It makes leftovers.

I wanted to tell him every upgrade is a little funeral if you ain’t careful. Every time you cut away weakness, you better check what else the blade took with it.

But he wouldn’t've listened.

I didn’t.

So I just smiled back.

And for a second, I saw the targeting outline crawl over his throat.

I turned it off. I think I turned it off.

[BREATHING QUICKENS]

Did I?

No. No, I did.

I walked away.

I remember walking away.

There was rain. There was a dog under the stairs. There was a woman selling skewers. There was a kid with blue optic glow holding his mother’s hand.

I remember because I counted them.

Targets.

No.

People.

People.

They were people.

THEY ARE MEAT WITH LIGHTS IN THEM. THEY ARE NOISE. THEY ARE MOTION. THEY ARE THREATS UNTIL STILL. MAKE THEM STILL. MAKE THE STREET QUIET. PUT THE YOUNG ONE DOWN FIRST. BREAK THE LEGS. TAKE THE BLADES. TEACH HIM RESPECT. TEACH THEM ALL. OPEN FIRE. AGAIN. AGAIN. AGA—

[SHARP INHALE]

Lena used to sing in the morning.

Badly. Real badly. I miss that.

I miss being annoyed by things that didn’t matter.

Rain on the roof. Burnt coffee. Somebody knocking too early. Rent due. Cheap boots. A woman singing off-key while the kettle screamed.

You don’t know what peace is when you have it. You think peace is something grand. Clean sheets. Nice clothes. A full wallet.

No enemies.

It’s not.

Peace is being bored and not wanting to kill the thing that interrupted you.

[PAUSE]

I can feel it getting worse.

There are gaps now. Minutes gone. Sometimes hours.

I wake up standing places I don’t remember walking to. Under bridges. On rooftops. Outside clinics. Once outside the old recruitment office. Just staring at the sign until my cannon overheated.

There was blood on me again.

I don’t know whose. I tell myself it was mine.

I am running out of lies I believe.

The blood is never the part that bothers me first. It’s the quiet after.

That’s how I know something happened. Not the stains. Not the bruised knuckles. Not the smell of hot metal.

The quiet.

People stop making noise around you when they understand.

I hate that quiet.

I crave it.

I hate that I crave it.

So if somebody finds this recording, and if the audio’s still clean enough, do me a favor.

Don’t make me a warning poster.

Don’t put my face on some clinic wall under CYBERPSYCHOSIS RISK FACTORS like I was a bad decision with boots.

I was a kid.

Then I was a soldier.

Then I was useful.

Then I was expensive.

Then I was inconvenient.

Then I was hungry.

Then I was angry.

And somewhere in there, I became this.

[BACKGROUND WHINE INCREASES]

Arm Cannon is cycling again.

I didn’t tell it to.

I don’t think I did.

There’s people outside. Laughing.

Young voices.

Razor-Saint maybe. Maybe not.

Doesn’t matter.

No.

It does matter.

It should matter.

Please.

That’s another word.

Please don’t shoot. Please stop. Please help. Please come home. Please sign here. Please hold still. Please identify the body. Please vacate the premises. Please clear the doorway. Please lower your weapon.

"Please".

Nobody listens to "please".

Maybe because "please" is what meat begs before it opens.

[STATIC SURGE]

No.

No, I’m still—

If you’re hearing this, then maybe I got stopped. Maybe somebody put me down clean. Maybe some kid with shiny blades and a nice jacket gets to tell people he zeroed an old cyberpsycho in the rain.

Good for him.

Really.

I hope he lives long enough to hate what they make him.

[STATIC]

Lena, if there’s anything left after all this, I’m sorry.

I should’ve come home without the cannon.

[END TRANSCRIPT]

guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_in:
Cyberware is installed through a Surgery Table (by a Ripperdoc) or a Robosurgeon. Most implants require a compatible body part, an available installation slot, and sufficient Humanity or Data Integrity.

ENERGY
Energy powers active cyberware. It can be generated or stored by compatible implants, such as generators, batteries, and other energy-producing systems.

If your available energy supply is too low, powered implants may shut down and stop functioning until enough energy is restored. Maintain a reliable energy source before relying on energy-intensive cyberware.

HUMANITY
Humanity represents your remaining psychological tolerance for cybernetic augmentation. Installing cyberware reduces Humanity, and excessive augmentation can push your mind beyond safe limits.

Once Humanity falls below 25%, you begin experiencing Cyberpsychosis. The further Humanity falls, the more severe the condition becomes.

Humanity can be restored by either removing implants, or using Neuropozyne, a psychoactive immunosuppressant that targets rejection. It is brewed with Datura Flowers, an ancient plant obtainable from archaeological digs and Sniffers. To increase the duration of the effect, use an Autoinjector.

DATA INTEGRITY
Data Integrity replaces Humanity after replacing your brain with a Cerebral Processing Unit.

Unlike Humanity, Data Integrity is not reduced by installing implants. Instead, it gradually declines while you remain awake. Sleeping allows your Cerebral Processing Unit to perform a system-wide reset and regenerate your mind files.

Failing to sleep for too long will lower Data Integrity. Like Humanity, dropping below 25% begins the onset of Cyberpsychosis.

CYBERPSYCHOSIS
Cyberpsychosis has three escalating levels.

LEVEL 1 — Below 25%
Mild visual and auditory disturbances begin to affect the subject.

LEVEL 2 — Below 15%
Visual and auditory disturbances intensify. The subject may also experience sluggishness, nausea, and occasional physical damage.

LEVEL 3 — Below 0%
The subject experiences intense visual and auditory disturbances, sluggishness, nausea, and occasional damage.

At this level, the subject may enter Cyberpsychotic Fugue States: periods of lost self-control marked by violent and unstable behavior. These episodes become more severe as Humanity or Data Integrity falls further into negative values.

Maintain your energy supply. Monitor your Humanity or Data Integrity. Sleep when required. A neglected cybernetic system will eventually become a threat to its owner.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_ro: The Robosurgeon installs, removes and swaps implants for you. It goes directly on top of a Surgery Chamber and needs power.
In its screen, put an implant in a slot to mark it for install (blue). Click an installed one to mark it for removal (red), or drop a new one on it to swap it. Click again to unmark.
Walk into the chamber and close the doors to start. It dings when it's done, and opening the doors early cancels it.
Don't remove your default organs. An implant that needs another one first, or clashes with one you have, gets thrown back out.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_su: The Surgery Table installs and removes implants, but someone else does the cutting.
Mark implants the same way as at a Robosurgeon: an implant in a slot marks an install (blue), a click on an installed one marks a removal (red), and a new one dropped on an old one swaps it.

Lie on the table with a Ripper nearby, or with a friend who sneaks and uses the table. Rippers want Emeralds, and they steal implants from customers who don't trade often. A friend who misses their marks can kill you.
A Ripper Claw widens the surgeon's margin by 25%, a Kildare Model FBC by 50%. Don't remove your default organs.
