guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_be:
This document catalogs known cybernetic organisms encountered across the overworld, the Nether, and hostile settlements. Entries are based on field observation, recovered implant data, and post-encounter anatomical analysis.

The listed subjects should be considered unstable unless otherwise noted. Cybernetic augmentation does not inherently produce aggression, but trauma, incompatible hardware, failed maintenance, neurological degradation, and hostile programming frequently result in dangerous behavior.

CYBERZOMBIE
Classification: Undead Cybernetic Human
Threat Level: Moderate
Disposition: Hostile

Cyberzombies are deceased or reanimated human subjects whose bodies retain enough functional cybernetic hardware to remain mobile after biological death. Their implants continue to supply mechanical assistance to damaged musculature, maintain limited coordination, and compensate for organ failure that would otherwise render the subject immobile.

Unlike conventional zombies, Cyberzombies exhibit abnormal durability and more consistent locomotion. This is likely caused by reinforced skeletal components, artificial muscle bundles, and residual power stored within implanted systems. Their behavior remains largely instinctive: they pursue living targets, respond to nearby movement, and attack through blunt force rather than deliberate tactical behavior.

Field observations suggest that many Cyberzombies were not originally intended for combat. Their augmentation appears to be civilian, industrial, medical, or survival-oriented hardware repurposed by post-mortem reanimation. Despite this, their implants make them significantly more dangerous than typical undead.

CYBERSKELETON
Classification: Undead Cybernetic Human, Advanced Decomposition State
Threat Level: High
Disposition: Hostile

Cyberskeletons are heavily decomposed Cyberzombies whose external tissue has deteriorated to the point that only skeletal structure, mechanical implants, and surviving connective hardware remain. Their lack of skin and muscle tissue exposes much of their cybernetic framework.

Despite appearing more fragile than Cyberzombies, Cyberskeletons are often more dangerous. Their remaining body mass is lower, allowing implanted mechanical systems to move the subject with greater speed and efficiency. Many specimens also retain ranged-combat capability, suggesting that their neural remnants or embedded targeting systems preserve more complex combat behaviors than those found in ordinary undead.

SMASHER
Classification: Heavily Augmented Illager
Threat Level: Extreme
Disposition: Hostile

Smashers are Illager combat subjects transformed through extreme cybernetic augmentation. Their bodies have been rebuilt around heavy industrial and military-grade implants, producing immense physical strength, impact resistance, and close-range destructive capability.

A Smasher’s skeletal system is reinforced beyond normal biological limits, while artificial musculature and hydraulic assist systems allow it to strike with crushing force. Most observed specimens possess heavily modified arms, reinforced torsos, and extensive neurological hardware intended to suppress pain response and increase aggression.

The psychological condition of Smashers is unstable. Their augmentation appears to prioritize combat output over long-term mental integrity. This often results in violent fixation, reduced self-preservation, and an inability to disengage once a target has been selected.

Smashers should not be treated as ordinary Illagers. Their combat behavior resembles that of a mobile breaching weapon: they close distance rapidly, seize targets, and rely on overwhelming physical force.

RIPPER
Classification: Lightly Augmented Illager Surgical Specialist
Threat Level: Low
Disposition: Neutral

Rippers are Illager surgical specialists equipped with compact cybernetic enhancements intended for precision work. Their modifications are less extensive than those found in Smashers.

They are fully neutral and will perform surgery on anything willing to pay. If the patient is not seen as lucrative, the Ripper may steal implants while the patient is under. To improve relations, trading is a must.

HOGBOY
Classification: Cyberpiglin Nether Ganger
Threat Level: None
Disposition: Passive

HogBoys are cybernetically augmented piglins associated with Nether ganger culture. Unlike more aggressive cyberpiglin groups, HogBoys are generally cooperative toward outsiders and are often willing to coexist, trade, or travel alongside other inhabitants of the Nether.

Their modifications tend to be practical rather than militarized. Common implants include heat-resistant plating, reinforced limbs, environmental protection systems, and utility cybernetics designed for survival in lava-adjacent environments, hostile terrain, and resource-scarce settlements.

HogBoys frequently display visible faction markings, improvised cybernetic repairs, and decorative modifications. Their implants may be mismatched, scavenged, or customized, reflecting the decentralized nature of Nether ganger engineering.

Gang Color: Blue

PUNKLIN
Classification: Cyberpiglin Nether Ganger, Aggressive Faction
Threat Level: Moderate
Disposition: Neutral

Punklins are aggressive cyberpiglin gangers distinguished by improvised combat cybernetics, faction-oriented modifications, and a strong tendency toward territorial violence. Their augmentations are often assembled from scavenged military hardware, industrial components, damaged implants, and stolen technological equipment.

Unlike the more community-oriented HogBoys, Punklins exhibit openly antagonistic behavior toward anything with enough implants. Their combat style is erratic, aggressive, and frequently theatrical, favoring intimidation, sudden attacks, and overwhelming numbers. They seem to have no problem ripping implants from enemies. They are so obsessed with cyberware and gold that they will stop attacking if you drop some.

Punklin implants commonly emphasize mobility, weapon handling, and intimidation rather than long-term reliability. This creates a dangerous combination: they may be physically less stable than military-grade subjects, but their willingness to take risks makes them unpredictable.

Many Punklins appear to view augmentation as both a survival tool and a social symbol. Visible gold implants, fresh plating, and improvised upgrades may indicate status within their faction.

Gang Color: Purple

PIGSTROM
Classification: Cyberpiglin Nether Ganger, Cyberpsychotic Subjects
Threat Level: Extreme
Disposition: Hostile

Pigstroms are cyberpiglin subjects suffering from severe cybernetic instability and apparent cyberpsychosis. Their augmentation exceeds the practical limits of their biological and psychological tolerance, resulting in violent behavioral collapse, impaired judgment, and extreme aggression.

Unlike Punklins, whose hostility is often organized around factional identity or territorial control, Pigstroms are erratic and indiscriminate. They may attack enemies, nearby creatures, or environmental targets with little apparent distinction. Like Punklins, they are so obsessed with cyberware that they will stop attacking if you drop some.

Their implants are frequently overdriven, damaged, or poorly maintained. Excessive augmentation may produce visible mechanical strain, unstable movement patterns, power surges, and irregular combat behavior. Some specimens demonstrate bursts of speed, strength, or endurance beyond what their frame should safely support.

Pigstroms represent the most dangerous outcome of unmanaged cybernetic escalation: a subject whose body continues functioning while its mind has lost the ability to regulate aggression, fear, or restraint.

Gang Color: Red
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_cy: Cyberdeck
The ultimate hacking tool

The Cyberdeck is an advanced piece of security technology, capable of sending malicious code packets to cybernetic targets and individuals. To use it, you first need to acquire Quickhacks and install them onto your Cyberdeck. Quickhacks are transmittable programs that can be used to perform tasks within the code controlling a target's augments.

Each Quickhack comes with its own success rate. Some programs contain large amounts of code, and the larger the code packet, the less likely it is to successfully transmit. This success rate can be further disrupted if the target has an ICE Defense Protocol installed, which has a 75% chance to interrupt transmission.

To install Quickhacks, check your cyberdeck model for its controls. Open the slots menu and input up to 4 suitable Quickhacks. When your chosen Quickhacks are installed, you can open the Quickhack selection menu, and scroll through the installed Quickhacks to select one. While hovering over your chosen target, select the desired program to transmit and run it.

When your program is deployed on a target, your Cyberdeck will alert you to its success or failure, and even let you know if the target disrupted deployment with an ICE Defense Protocol. Similarly however, it's important to note that the target will also be made aware of the attempt, successful or not, as their systems alert them to the presence of foreign code. Quickhacks cannot successfully deploy if the target does not have implants with affectable systems (e.g.: you cannot deploy Scramble.exe on a target that does not have Cyberlegs or a Linear Frame).
After deployment, your Cyberdeck will need to cool down to avoid synapse burnout. Because of this a 10 second cooldown period will initiate, during which you cannot cast code packets.

OVERHEAT.EXE
Success Rate: 75%
Affected Systems: Any
Overheats processors to ignite augments and burn the target from the inside out.

REBOOT.EXE
Success Rate: 65%
Affected Systems: Any
Reboots all systems, briefly causing a systemwide shutdown from a lack of energy acceptance.

SCRAMBLE.EXE
Success Rate: 80%
Affected Systems: Cyberlegs, Linear Frame
Scrambles motor control and directional capabilities, causing targets to spin in circles.

OPTIC_MALFUNCTION.EXE
Success Rate: 80%
Affected Systems: Cybereyes
Short-circuits cyberoptics, causing the target to temporarily go blind while the optic system tries to reroute power.

DRAIN.EXE
Success Rate: 75%
Affected Systems: Any
Makes cyberware energy distribution and consumption as inefficient as possible, doubling energy drain for a short time.

BEHIND_YOU.EXE
Success Rate: 95%
Affected Systems: Brain Implants
An auditory processing bug that plays hostile audio behind the target.

CYBERPSYCHOSIS.EXE
Success Rate: 15%
Affected Systems: Any
Temporarily shuts down input guards, draining 75% of the target's humanity, and virtually guaranteeing cyberpsychosis.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_ha:
Enchantment Name: Harvester
Classification: Weapon Enchantment

The first confirmed instance of the Harvester enchantment was recovered from an abandoned warehouse containing extensive evidence of human butchery for black market organ trades. The enchantment was bound to an iron axe found near the remains.

Initial examination suggests that Harvester grants an abnormal degree of cutting precision. Weapons carrying the enchantment appear capable of separating organs, muscle tissue, and other biological material with uncanny surgical accuracy, even when used through uncontrolled or improvised swings. The effect does not appear to improve the wielder’s skill, judgment, or anatomical knowledge. Rather, the weapon itself seems to guide the cut, allowing tissue to be removed with a level of finesse comparable to that of a trained surgical professional.
Further testing is not recommended on living human subjects.

NOTE:
A farmer using a weapon enchanted with Harvester reported obtaining an unidentified organ while slaughtering sheep. Subsequent examination identified the organ as a modified ovine stomach, removed in an unusually complete and transplantable condition. The Harvester enchantment appears to preserve or alter the extracted stomach in a way that permits successful transplantation into a human subject.

Human recipients of the Grassfed Stomach demonstrate the ability to consume grass directly from the ground and derive substantial nutrition from raw wheat. However, this adaptation comes with a severe dietary limitation: subjects become unable to consume conventional food sources.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.cyber_cy: Cyberchems
Chemical modifiers and addiction

Cyberchems are chemical modifiers designed to interact with and augment biology. They can grant massive buffs alongside massive debuffs, but the majority can have lasting effects that may make it not entirely worth it.

Addiction is the most notable lasting side effect for many of these chemicals. It can affect the body for 7 days, leaving the afflicted slow, weak, and unable to fight or defend themselves. Addiction can be cleared by consuming more of the addictive chemicals that caused the affliction in the first place. The most noticeable trait is shaking and convulsions.

Each of the following can be used in an Autoinjector to increase the effect's duration to a full day (with the exception of Warp, which has no added benefit when used as an injectable). Autoinjectors can also be filled with any other potion to increase its level by +1. Autoinjectors can be applied to others by sneaking and holding use on them, or applied to yourself by holding use.

ROID
This chemical grants users immense strength and speed, and increases the user's size.
Each dose has a 10% chance to inflict the user with Addiction.
-10 Humanity for the first dose, and -5 for every subsequent dose.
Brewed from Ravager Tendons.

STIM
This chemical grants users a chance to dodge incoming damage, and can be scaled up with multiple doses. Scalability caps at 4 doses (1 dose = 20%, 4 doses = 90%).
Each dose has a 10% chance to inflict the user with Addiction.
-5 Humanity per dose.
Brewed from Redstone.

BLACK LACE
This chemical increases durability and grants an immunity to wither, but obscures health from the user. When the effect wears off, the user will have occasional bouts of wither.
Each dose has a 10% chance to inflict the user with Addiction.
-15 Humanity for the first dose, and -5 for every subsequent dose.
Brewed from a Wither Skeleton Skull.

IMMUNOBOOST
This chemical negates all negative effects at the cost of humanity by overexciting the immune system. Does not typically pair well with implants.
-25 Humanity per dose.
Brewed from a Glistering Melon Slice.

WARP
This chemical immediately teleports the user somewhere randomly within a 64x64 grid. Might make the user nauseous.
Brewed from an Ender Pearl.

NEUROPOZYNE
This chemical grants humanity and alleviates cyberpsychosis by suppressing immune responses. If more than 4 doses are administered, the user will begin to experience nausea.
+25 Humanity per dose.
Brewed from a Datura Flower.

ADDICTOL
This chemical makes the user weak, nauseous, and incapable of fighting for a full day, but when the effect clears, it takes the Addiction effect with it.
Brewed from a Ghast Tear.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.cyberware: The manuals that come with cyberware. Read them before the surgery.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_scr: Cyberzombies and Cyberskeletons carry old implants, and strongholds hide a few more. Get your hands on one.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_ben: Build a Cyberware Bench. It crafts new implants and takes scavenged ones apart for parts.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_chr: Craft your first implant at the Cyberware Bench.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_sur: Build a Surgery Table. A Ripper will operate on you for emeralds, or a friend can do the cutting.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_neu: Every implant costs Humanity, and running out is bad news. A Neuropozyne Autoinjector brings some back. Antazon sells them.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_sni: Install Retractable Claws. They need adamantium.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_web: Graft a cobweb and some web fluid onto an arm at the Grafting Table.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_rob: Build a Robosurgeon over a Surgery Chamber and you won’t need a Ripper. Its Netherite QPU turns up in bastions, fortresses and trial vaults.
task.integrated_boogaloo.cybernetics_ful: Go all the way with a full-body conversion.
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_tread: Build a Treadmill and get something running on it. Pigs work. An ant makes about thirty times the power.
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_const: Build a Shell Constructor, then right-click it with an empty hand to give it a sample. The sample takes eight hearts, so don't do it at half health.
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_stora: Build a Shell Storage and keep it powered. A redstone signal is enough. If the power cuts out for more than ten seconds, the body inside dies.
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_first: Walk into a powered storage and pick a shell. Your old body stays behind with everything it was carrying.
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_long_: Leave a shell in another dimension, then move into it from home.
Move into a shell in another dimension
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_zero_: Upgrade a Shell Storage so it runs without power. The body inside never decays.
task.integrated_boogaloo.body_shop_manua: Build a Manual Shell Storage. You never wake up in it by accident when you die, so it's a good place for a mining body or one parked far from home.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.body_sho: A shell is a spare body grown from your own sample, with its own inventory, armor, experience and health.
Give a Shell Constructor a sample with an empty hand and power it. Something running on a Treadmill beside it works: a pig grows a shell in about five minutes, a worker ant in ten seconds.
Keep a Shell Storage powered with redstone and walk in while the doors are open to switch bodies.
Die in a shell and you wake up in the next one. It doesn't count as a death, but the body you left drops what it carried. Dying in your original body is a normal death.
Implants stay with the body they were put in. A Manual Shell Storage is never picked for you when you die.
computer.integrated_boogaloo.product.cri: A home gym for pigs, wolves and ants. Hooks up to anything that runs on power. Animal not included.
Hooked it up to the old cloning machine. Grim won't go near it, but the pig has never looked better!!
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.chess.des: Four opponents, from easy to very patient.
task.integrated_boogaloo.pastel_blueston: Bluestone Dike recharges to absorb damage and lets you cross force-field gates. Equip a Ring or Belt and let at least one charge build up.
Gain a charge of Bluestone Dike
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.pastel_b: Bluestone Dike absorbs incoming damage and recharges over time; charged protection lets you pass force-field gates in Preservation Ruins and Imbrifer vaults.
The Ring adds capacity and speeds charging, while the Belt adds capacity and shortens the recovery delay after a hit.
Blue Ink in a Color Picker increases the protection supplied by the equipment.
The Bluestone Dike Core doubles protection from other sources and improves recovery, but provides no shield on its own.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.antazon_a: A catalog that isn't on the main site. No returns.
computer.integrated_boogaloo.product.mat: Four polished Topaz blocks, or thirty-six shards if you unpack them.
Four polished Citrine blocks, or thirty-six shards if you unpack them.
Four polished Amethyst blocks, or thirty-six shards if you unpack them.
Four polished Moonstone blocks, or thirty-six shards if you unpack them.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_drag: Wild dragons are won over with food. Stand 12 to 16 blocks away with empty hands, drop its food within five blocks of you and keep still while it eats.
Wait a few seconds and feed it again. When it's ready, face its head and hold use with an empty hand.
Eggs only warm up once placed near torches, a lit campfire or lava. Whoever places one owns the hatchling.
Only a grown Broad Wing takes a Dragon Saddle. The Dragon Roster calls your dragons back from anywhere, even another dimension.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_nigh: The rarest of the small dragons. Night Furies live high in cold mountains, groves and windswept hills and mostly come out after dark.
They watch strangers for a long time before coming close. Keep calm, keep your hands empty and offer cod.
Fastest thing in the sky once it's yours. Its plasma blast glows and hums while it charges, then hits very hard.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_dead: Bright, proud and spiky, with a beaked snout and a clubbed tail. Nadders hunt the forests and taiga.
They take raw chicken, but wait at least twelve seconds between feeds. Approach where it can see you.
The tail fires venomous spines with scary accuracy, so never stand behind one. A ridden Nadder breathes fire for as long as you hold the attack, and can spit spines or bite.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_gron: A round, rock-skinned dragon with tiny wings that beat much faster than they should. Gronckles live on stony peaks, mountains and rocky shores.
Wild ones eat dropped raw iron or cobblestone, but only while standing on solid ground. Feed your own raw iron by hand to heal it, and give two adults copper ore to breed them.
Ridden, it lobs molten rock after a short windup. The blast hurts everything it lands on but leaves the ground alone.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_red_: A dragon the size of a mountain, asleep in the volcano on Dragon Island. The Hooligans talk about more than one island, and a Red Death sleeps on every one.
She stays asleep until something hits her. Then she bites, and she can swallow a person whole, and she breathes fire hot enough to leave nothing.
When she roars, her nest answers. Nadders and Gronckles first, and once she's hurt badly enough, a full-grown Monstrous Nightmare. When she drags in a huge breath, hit her hard before she lets it go.
Dr. T: Her fangs are the size of a door! I need one for Big Bertha.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_hool: Hooligans are Vikings. Their villages sit in taiga, snowy plains and cold, stony shores, and the coastal ones have docks, longships and a catapult tower.
They trade for emeralds: axes, maces, round shields, bolas, Dragon Saddles, food and notes on disks. Hiccup's Dagger turns up now and then.
A thrown bola wraps up whatever it hits. Hooligans use them on wild dragons that wander too close.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.survey_d: Volcanic islands far out in deep ocean behind rings of sea stacks, each with a Red Death asleep in the crater. Shows the nearest one.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_dr: Hooligan notes on taming, hatching and riding small dragons.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_ni: Everything the Hooligans know about Night Furies. It's a short disk.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_de: Hooligan notes on the Deadly Nadder.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_he: Directions to Dragon Island. The Hooligans won't go themselves.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_mons: The biggest dragon the Hooligans will talk about, after the Red Death herself. A Monstrous Nightmare sleeps on a pile of gold out in the hot, dry country and wakes up in a bad mood.
When it fights it sets its own hide on fire. The old Vikings say you never chase one into a forest and you never fight one on top of its gold.
A blade forged in ice cuts it deepest. The Hooligans pay well for its bones and scales, and a Nightmare skull will buy you a lot of goodwill in any great hall.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_snow: Snow Wraiths hunt the frozen north, right on the Hooligans' doorstep. They're as white as the snow they hide in, and you rarely hear one coming.
Its breath doesn't burn you. It freezes you solid where you stand, so keep moving and don't fight one out on open ice.
Fire is what it hates, and a blade forged in fire does it real harm. Most villages keep a Wraith skull beside the fire in the great hall to remind the children where not to wander.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.bda_skri: The Skrill rides storms. It nests in swamps, jungles and the red badlands, and you hear the thunder well before you see it.
It breathes lightning and rarely misses. Hooligans take off their iron helmets before they go after one, and they still come home short a few people.
A blade forged with Skrill lightning bites both of the other two. Against the Skrill itself there's no trick, so bring friends.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_mo: Hooligan notes on hunting Monstrous Nightmares.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_sn: Hooligan notes on hunting Snow Wraiths.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.viking_sk: Hooligan notes on hunting the Skrill.
task.integrated_boogaloo.dragon_academy_: First Offering
Get a wild dragon to accept food from you.
Small dragons come round slowly. Stand well back with empty hands, drop the food it likes and keep still while it comes over to eat.
Forbidden Friendship
Tame a dragon.
Keep feeding it until it trusts you, then face its head and hold use with an empty hand.
Dragon Rider
Saddle and ride a grown dragon.
Only a full-grown Broad Wing takes a Dragon Saddle. Hatchlings and Short Wings have to wait.
Test Drive
Fly 100 blocks on your dragon without touching down.
Take it up high and keep it there.
Tiny Tooth
Hatch a dragon egg.
Eggs only warm up next to torches, a lit campfire or lava. A splash of Fire Dragon Blood on the shell speeds things up a lot.
Broad Wing
Raise a dragon you hatched all the way to adulthood.
Tiny Tooth, then Short Wing, then Broad Wing. Hoard dragon flesh heals a hurt one fast.
We Have Dragons
Tame a Night Fury, a Deadly Nadder and a Gronckle.
A grown, tame Nadder or Gronckle told to sit near a Dragon Forge will keep a fire forge going, and a Night Fury a lightning one. Slower than a hoard dragon, but they never try to eat you.
Welcome to Berk
Find a Hooligan village.
Vikings live up in the taiga, the snowy plains and along cold, stony coasts. They know more about dragons than anyone.
Hooligan Trader
Trade with a Hooligan.
Hooligans buy dragon bone, flesh, scales and skulls, and they sell their notes on floppy disks.
I Have Brought Down This Mighty Beast
Catch a wild dragon with a bola.
A bola wraps up a small dragon for a good while. A full-grown hoard dragon shrugs it off in a couple of seconds, but that can be enough.
Helheim's Gate
Buy the Helheim's Gate disk from a Hooligan.
Only some Hooligans will sell it, and it costs a stack of emeralds. It points the way to Dragon Island.
Dragon Island
Reach Dragon Island.
Way out in deep ocean, behind a ring of sea stacks. Don't wake anything you can't handle.
The Red Death
Help bring down the Red Death.
She calls her nest when she roars, and late in the fight a full-grown Monstrous Nightmare answers. Everyone who fought her gets a fang.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.survey_h: Viking villages up in the taiga, the snowy plains and along cold coasts, most of them with docks and longships. Shows the nearest one.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.disk.survey_vi: Points the way to the nearest Hooligan village.
integrated_boogaloo.waystones.no_dimensi: Waystones can't reach into another dimension.
task.integrated_boogaloo.witchery_warp_s: Ender Dew from the Distillery, amethyst shards and an Attuned Amethyst.
task.integrated_boogaloo.witchery_waysto: Every village has a waystone, but you can build your own.
task.integrated_boogaloo.witchery_return: Whiff of Magic, Ender Dew and paper. Read one to go back to the last waystone you activated.
task.integrated_boogaloo.witchery_warp_s: Ender Dew around a Spirit of Otherwhere from the cauldron. Read one to pick any waystone you've activated.
guide.integrated_boogaloo.entry.tech_for: Force fields run on Fortron, which a Coercion Deriver makes from power. Machines set to the same frequency share it, and a Fortron Capacitor stores it and passes it along.
A Projector takes a mode for the shape and modules for size and extras. It burns Fortron every second it's on, and bigger fields and heavier modules burn more.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_for: A Coercion Deriver turns power into Fortron, the energy force fields run on. Hook it up to a generator.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_bub: Give a Projector a mode and some Scale Modules, then switch it on. Machines on the same frequency share Fortron, so it draws from your Deriver.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_sha: Swap the cube for a sphere, a tube or a pyramid. Bigger fields burn more Fortron every second, so keep an eye on the gauge.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_sta: A Fortron Capacitor stores Fortron and sends it to every machine on its frequency. Sneak and use a Frequency Card to roll a new one.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_kee: An Interdiction Matrix guards the ground around your field, and its modules decide what happens to anyone who walks in. Hand out ID Cards at a Biometric Identifier so it knows who's allowed.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_now: A Camouflage Module makes the field look like a block of your choice. Handy if you'd rather people didn't know it's there.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_cop: Right-click two corners of a build with a Custom Mode, then sneak and right-click to save it. Load it into a Projector and the field copies the shape.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_for: With a Disintegration Module the field breaks every block it passes through. Add a Collection Module to keep what falls out.
task.integrated_boogaloo.locked_down_rig: A Biometric Identifier also takes keycards and Allowlist Modules, and anyone carrying that keycard or on that list gets the rights you give it. A Denylist Module shuts its players out.
computer.integrated_boogaloo.product.gea: Took the hammer off and screwed this on. Best hand I've had in years, and now I can fry eggs.

Bought one. Came back the next hour and bought another.
We have a mountain of this at home.
